title: Newspaper Report Regarding The Stoning Of A Girl Rider By Chinese Villagers On Great Western Road

page_data.en:
Fm. 3
G. 350-1-34

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
S. 1, Special Branch.
REPORT
File No. B. REGISTRY.
D
Date February 11, 19 35.

Subject (in full) Newspaper report regarding the stoning of a girl rider
by Chinese villagers on Great Western Road.

Made by J.S. McKeown Forwarded by H. Cruickshank

Regarding the attached newspaper cutting dealing
with the stoning of a foreign girl rider on Great Western
Road on February 4, after interviewing an eye-witness and
officers of Bubbling Well Station who investigated the case,
I have to state that the report though exaggerated, was
founded on fact.

Mr. J.H. Koch (Swiss) of Huber and Co., 136 Canton
Road, who witnessed and was involved in the incident gave
the following version.

At about 2 p.m. February 4, accompanied by Mr. E.R.
Mason of the North China Daily News, he was walking along
Great Western Road, and when approaching the junction of
Great Western and Hungjao Roads, observed two foreign girls,
one mounted and one on foot, surrounded by a crowd of Chinese,
one of whom was holding a pony. Upon his inquiring the cause
of the trouble, one of the girls stated that she had been
thrown, and her pony had been captured by a Chinese who was
demanding $10 which she refused to pay. Mr. Koch then asked
the Chinese to return the pony. Upon the latter refusing to
comply with the request, Mr. Koch struck him on the mouth and
took the pony from him. He was assisting the girl to mount
when someone in the crowd threw a stone which struck her on
the back of the head. With the assistance of Mr. Mason, the
injured girl was placed in a ricsha, and telling her companion
who had remained in the saddle to ride on ahead, the two men
accompanied the injured girl to the house of Mr. Tackaberry,
some little distance away. No more stones were thrown and
the attitude of the crowd was not menacing. A friend of
Mr. Tackaberry dressed the wound which was not a serious one,

上海公共租界工部局警务处。
S. 1，特务科。
报告
档案号 B. 登记处。
D
日期 1935年2月11日。

主题（全称） 关于大西路一名女骑手被中国村民投石袭击的报纸报道。

制作人 J.S. McKeown 转呈人 H. Cruickshank

关于所附剪报中提及的2月4日在大西路发生的外国女骑手被投石袭击一事，经询问目击者及调查此案的静安寺捕房警官后，本人须声明，该报道虽有夸大，但确有其事。

广东路136号 Huber 公司的 J.H. Koch 先生（瑞士籍）是事件的目击者及当事人，他提供了以下经过。

2月4日下午2时许，他由《字林西报》的 E.R. Mason 先生陪同，沿大西路行走。当接近大西路与虹桥路交界处时，看见两名外国女子，一人骑在马上，一人在步行，被一群中国人包围，其中一人牵着一匹小马。当他询问骚乱原因时，其中一名女子称她已从马上摔下，她的小马被一名中国人扣留，此人索要10美元，被她拒绝。Koch 先生随即要求该中国人归还小马。在该人拒绝配合后，Koch 先生击打其嘴部，并从小马主人手中夺回小马。正当他协助该女子重新上马时，人群中有人投掷石块，击中该女子后脑。在 Mason 先生的协助下，受伤女子被安置在一辆人力车中，并告知留在马鞍上的同伴先行骑行离开，随后两人陪同受伤女子前往不远处的 Tackaberry 先生寓所。此后未再有人投掷石块，人群的态度也不具威胁性。Tackaberry 先生的一位朋友为伤口进行了包扎，伤势并不严重，

after which the two girls were conveyed by car to the junction
of Avenue Joffre and Route Doumer, and alighted there after
thanking their rescuers. Beyond the fact that they were
Russians and both young, neither Mr. Koch nor the other
persons involved could give any information regarding the
names and addresses of the girls and inquiries by the
undersigned have failed to establish their identity. The two
ponies were taken back to a Chinese stable by a mafoo who had
followed the girls.

Officers of Bubbling Well Station who made
investigations at the scene of the incident substantiate
Mr. Koch's statement.

The newspaper report to the effect that the girls
were mobbed is exaggerated. The payment of a sum of money
as a reward to the person who captures a runaway pony is a
custom to which most riders conform, and the Chinese in this
case was naturally reluctant to return the pony without
receiving the reward. The throwing of the stone followed
the impetuous action of Mr. Koch, and the newspaper report
does not include a record of this incident.

（批：J.R.）

随后两名女子乘车前往霞飞路与杜美路交界处，下车后向施救者致谢。除了知道她们是俄罗斯人且都很年轻外，Koch 先生及其他相关人员均无法提供这两名女子的姓名和地址，经下文签署人查询，亦未能确认其身份。两匹小马由一名跟随女子的马夫牵回一家中国马厩。

静安寺捕房在现场进行调查的警官证实了 Koch 先生的陈述。

报纸报道中称女孩们遭到暴民围攻的说法属于夸大。向捕获走失小马的人支付一笔酬金是大多数骑手遵循的惯例，本案中的中国人自然不愿在未收到酬金的情况下归还小马。投掷石块的行为是在 Koch 先生冲动行事之后发生的，而报纸报道中并未记录这一情节。

（批注：J.R.）

0987
THE NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS, WEDNESDAY, FEBRUARY 6, 1935

GIRLS MOBBED
OUT RIDING

Hungjao Road Villagers
Wound One

RESCUED BY TWO MEN

Mystery of Identity Not
Yet Solved

An ugly incident occurred shortly after the tiffin hour on Monday just off Hungjao Road, when two young foreign girls, out for an afternoon's riding, were attacked by a mob of Chinese villagers. They were rescued by two foreigners out for a stroll, who came on to the scene just as things were getting tense. One girl had her head badly cut by a flying stone.

How the incident started is not known. Messrs. E. R. Mason and J. L. Koch were walking along Hungjao Road and, near the corner where Warren and Great Western Roads join Hungjao Road, they saw one girl mounted, surrounded by a crowd of angry Chinese. On running forward, they found the second girl dismounted. The riderless pony was being led away by some Chinese. The two men immediately interfered, secured the pony, and were helping the young woman to mount again just as stones began to fly. One big one, hurled by one of the villagers, hit her on the back of the head, cutting it open. It knocked her off the pony again, practically unconscious.

Rickshaw Commandeered

Stones then began to fly in greater numbers, each of the four foreigners being hit, though without any damage. Fortunately a rickshaw was standing near. The men bundled the wounded girl into this and, while one secured the pony, they ran for the house of a friend, Mr. H. J. Tackaberry, not far away. The four reached the house in safety, though they were chased by the growing mob of Chinese.

The crowd became more and more threatening and a call was put in immediately to the Bubbling Well Station of the Shanghai Municipal Police. While this was being done, a nurse was summoned and the young woman's head was attended to and dressed. As she had regained consciousness she was put into a car and rushed to the city before the arrival of the police.

When the police arrived the villagers had scattered and, though every attempt was made to find the cause of the trouble and all evidence that could be secured was taken, very little was learned.

The two foreign girls, apparently eighteen or nineteen years of age, were unknown to any of their rescuers. In the general excitement their names were not ascertained.

（批：SI. Please verify and report, if true, a reference should be made to the incident in the monthly report.）
（签名）
（批：2/9 7/2）

0987
《字林西报》，1935年2月6日，星期三

少女外出骑马
遭暴民围攻

虹桥路村民
致一人受伤

两男子施以援手

身份之谜尚未解开

周一午餐时间刚过，在虹桥路附近发生了一起恶劣事件，两名外出进行下午骑马活动的外国年轻女子遭到一群中国村民的攻击。两名正在散步的外国人及时赶到现场，在局势趋于紧张之际将她们救出。其中一名女子的头部被飞来的石块严重砸伤。

事件起因尚不清楚。E. R. Mason 先生和 J. L. Koch 先生正沿着虹桥路行走，在华伦路和大西路汇入虹桥路的拐角附近，他们看到一名骑在马上的女孩被一群愤怒的中国人包围。上前查看后，他们发现第二名女孩已下马。那匹无主的小马正被几名中国人牵走。两人立即介入，控制住小马，并正在帮助那名年轻女子重新上马，此时石块开始飞来。其中一块大石头由一名村民掷出，击中她的后脑，导致头皮破裂。这使她再次从马上跌落，几乎失去知觉。

征用人力车

随后石块越扔越多，四名外国人每人都被击中，但未造成任何伤害。幸运的是，附近停着一辆人力车。男人们将受伤的女孩塞进车里，一人负责看好小马，其他人则跑向不远处的一位朋友 H. J. Tackaberry 先生的住所。四人安全抵达该住所，尽管身后有越来越多的中国暴民追赶。

人群变得越来越具有威胁性，当局立即致电上海公共租界工部局警务处静安寺捕房。在此期间，请来了一名护士，对年轻女子的头部伤口进行处理和包扎。由于她已恢复意识，在警察到达之前，她被送上汽车紧急送往市区。

当警察到达时，村民已四散奔逃，尽管当局尽力寻找骚乱原因并收集了所有能获取的证据，但所得甚微。

这两名外国女孩，年龄看似十八九岁，她们的施救者均不认识她们。在一片混乱中，未能查明她们的姓名。

（批注：SI. 请核实并报告，如属实，应在月度报告中提及此事件。）
（签名）
（批注：2/9 7/2）

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
S. 2, Special Demonstration, 1—
REPORT
Date February 12, 19 35.
Subject activities of A.S. Rybin, Suspected Soviet
Intelligence Agent.
Made by D.S. Tcherenshansky. Forwarded by S.B.Rm D..
* Contacts from
files attached.
Information has been received that A.S. Rybin, Soviet
citizen, who forms the subject of files D.6673 and I.O.7060/5,
is a Soviet intelligence agent. He was formerly employed with
the local branch of the Centrosojus. In May, 1933 he left
the service in that concern and soon afterwards joined the firm
"Bent Brothers", 755-61 Bubbling Well Road, which is reported
to be financed by Dalbank and to have several Soviet citizens
among its employees. It is believed that Rybin's employment
with the latter firm is only a camouflage of his real activities
in the capacity of a Soviet intelligence agent. In this
connection it is reported that Rybin recently approached a
certain Russian who formerly was connected with the Japanese
intelligence organs, and proposed to him to furnish information
regarding Japanese activities, stating that he was working for
the American Intelligence Service. On one occasion the
Russian received from Rybin $150 for a plan of a certain Japanese
factory and on another occasion $50 for a report on Japanese
activities in Mongolia.
Rybin resides at No. 1333 Avenue Joffre, Apt. H. He
is on intimate terms with one Nina Vladimirovna Gertz, Soviet
citizen, light opera singer by profession, who at present owns
the "Iris" Ladies Hat & Dress-making Salon, No. 216 Rue Cardinal
Mercier. It is reported that she is member of the RABIS (Union
of Soviet Stage Workers) and that she assists Rybin in his
intelligence work. Mrs. Gertz, who speaks English, German and
French languages, has a large clientele among foreign ladies.
* 25. 975
Jule

* 附件档案中的联系人。
已收到情报称，苏联公民 A.S. Rybin（涉及档案 D.6673 和 I.O.7060/5 的对象）是一名苏联情报人员。他此前受雇于中央消费合作总社（Centrosojus）本地分部。1933年5月，他离开该机构，不久后加入位于静安寺路755-61号的“Bent Brothers”公司，据报该公司由达利银行（Dalbank）资助，且员工中有数名苏联公民。据信，Rybin 在该公司的任职仅是其作为苏联情报人员真实活动的掩护。据此有报告称，Rybin 最近接触了一名曾与日本情报机关有关联的俄罗斯人，并向其提议提供有关日本活动的情报，声称自己为美国情报部门工作。有一次，该俄罗斯人因提供某家日本工厂的平面图而从 Rybin 处获得150美元；另一次，因提供关于日本在蒙古活动的报告而获得50美元。
Rybin 居住在霞飞路1333号 H 公寓。他与苏联公民 Nina Vladimirovna Gertz 关系密切，Gertz 职业为轻歌剧歌手，目前拥有位于梅白格路216号的“Iris”女士帽饰及裁缝沙龙。据报她是 RABIS（苏联舞台工作者联盟）成员，并协助 Rybin 进行情报工作。Gertz 夫人通晓英、德、法语，在外国女性顾客中拥有庞大的客户群。
* 25. 975
Jule
9/18

Through Rybin's acquaintance, Bent Bros. is being patronised
by the members of the U.S.S.R. Embassy, the Consulate-General
and other Soviet establishments.
